result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [CensoringType]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-enum} | greenwood description: The type of a Surv response, using R's type names. twitter-card: title: >- [CensoringType]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-enum} | greenwood description: The type of a Surv response, using R's type names. title: "[CensoringType]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-enum}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: The type of a Surv response, using R's type names. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The type of a `Surv` response, using R's type names. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_surv.py#L61-L196){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature CensoringType ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} - `RIGHT`: right-censored, `Surv(time, event)`. - `LEFT`: left-censored, `Surv(time, event, type="left")`. - `INTERVAL`: interval-censored, from `type="interval"` or `type="interval2"`. - `COUNTING`: counting-process `(start, stop]` intervals, `Surv(start, stop, event)`. - `MRIGHT`: multi-state right-censored, from a categorical `event=`. - `MCOUNTING`: multi-state counting-process, from a categorical `event=` with start times. A response reports its type through `Surv(...).type`. Because `CensoringType` is a `str` enum, it compares equal to R's type strings, such as `"right"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#155f08dc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from greenwood import CensoringType list(CensoringType) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [, , , , , ] ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [COUNTING](#COUNTING){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} | Counting-process data: each row is an interval `(start, stop]` at risk. | | [INTERVAL](#INTERVAL){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} | Interval data: each row may be exact, right-, left-, or interval-censored. | | [LEFT](#LEFT){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} | Left-censored data: the event may have happened before the recorded time. | | [MCOUNTING](#MCOUNTING){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} | Multi-state counting-process data: competing events with late entry. | | [MRIGHT](#MRIGHT){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} | Multi-state right-censored data: several kinds of event that compete. | | [RIGHT](#RIGHT){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} | Right-censored data: the event, if any, happens after the recorded time. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [COUNTING]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} ::: {.doc-subject} Counting-process data: each row is an interval `(start, stop]` at risk. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [COUNTING]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[["counting"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Used for late entry (left truncation), where subjects join the study after time zero, and for time-varying covariates, where each subject's follow-up is split into several rows. The status is `1` if the event happened at the stop time. `Surv()` infers it from a start time, a stop time, and a status: `Surv(time=start, time2=stop, event=d)`. The response's columns are `start`, `stop`, and `status`, as in R. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#1ad8a206 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw gw.Surv(time=[0, 2, 1], time2=[5, 6, 4], event=[1, 0, 1]).type ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ``` ::: ::: ### [INTERVAL]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} ::: {.doc-subject} Interval data: each row may be exact, right-, left-, or interval-censored. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [INTERVAL]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[["interval"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} ::: ::: {.doc-text} The most general single-event type. The status uses R's interval codes: `0` right-censored, `1` exact, `2` left-censored, and `3` interval-censored. It comes from `Surv(time, time2, event, type="interval")` with those codes, from `Surv(time=lower, time2=upper, type="interval2")` with open bounds marking censoring, or from `as_surv()` for an event-time vector that mixes codes in any other way. The response's columns are `time1`, `time2`, and `status`, as in R, where `time2` is `1` for rows that are not interval-censored. Fit it with `Turnbull`. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#0b3a6e94 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import greenwood as gw # The event happened in (1, 2], after 2, and in (3, 5] gw.Surv(time=[1, 2, 3], time2=[2, np.inf, 5], type="interval2").type ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ``` ::: ::: ### [LEFT]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} ::: {.doc-subject} Left-censored data: the event may have happened before the recorded time. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [LEFT]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[["left"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each row has a time and a status, using R's meaning: `1` is an event seen at that time, `0` means the event had already happened by then (left-censored). It must be asked for with `Surv(time=t, event=d, type="left")`, and `as_surv()` gives it for an event-time vector with only `"e"` and `"l"` codes. The response's columns are `time` and `status`, as in R. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#e0a72572 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw gw.Surv(time=[5, 6, 4], event=[1, 0, 1], type="left").type ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ``` ::: ::: ### [MCOUNTING]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} ::: {.doc-subject} Multi-state counting-process data: competing events with late entry. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [MCOUNTING]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[["mcounting"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} ::: ::: {.doc-text} The counting-process form of `MRIGHT`: each row is an interval `(start, stop]` at risk, and the status is `0` for censored or `k` for the `k`-th state name in `states`. `Surv()` gives this type for a start time, a stop time, and a categorical status, and `first_event()` gives it when `start=` is supplied. The response's columns are `start`, `stop`, and `status`, as in R. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#6917bf66 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd import greenwood as gw cause = pd.Categorical(["pcm", "censor"], categories=["censor", "pcm", "death"]) gw.Surv(time=[0, 2], time2=[5, 6], event=cause).type ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` ``` ::: ::: ### [MRIGHT]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} ::: {.doc-subject} Multi-state right-censored data: several kinds of event that compete. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [MRIGHT]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[["mright"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Used for competing risks, where each subject can experience at most one of several events (for example progression or death). The status is `0` for censored, or `k` for the `k`-th state name in the response's `states`. `Surv()` gives this type when the status is a categorical whose first category means censored, and `first_event()` builds it from one `(time, event)` column pair per endpoint. In a formula, write the status with `factor()`. The response's columns are `time` and `status`, as in R. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#d6c45cf6 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd import greenwood as gw cause = pd.Categorical(["pcm", "censor", "death"], categories=["censor", "pcm", "death"]) gw.Surv(time=[5, 6, 7], event=cause).type ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` ``` ::: ::: ### [RIGHT]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-constant} ::: {.doc-subject} Right-censored data: the event, if any, happens after the recorded time. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [RIGHT]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[["right"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} ::: ::: {.doc-text} The most common type. Each row has a follow-up time and a status: `1` if the event was seen at that time, `0` if the subject was event-free when last seen. `Surv()` infers it from a time and a status, `Surv(time=t, event=d)`, and `as_surv()` gives it for an event-time vector with only `"e"` and `"r"` codes. The response's columns are `time` and `status`, as in R. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#7d4672f1 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw gw.Surv(time=[5, 6, 4], event=[1, 0, 1]).type ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` ``` ::: :::
